summary: Front tower of the Caraquet range, a wooden light at Bas-Caraquet, New Brunswick, lit 24 September 1903 to lead ships through Caraquet Channel; the rear light was replaced in 2000.

lens.note: First lit with a seventh-order dioptric lens (1904 report). Current lens not in sources.

light.note: Fixed white when first lit (1904 report). Colour disputed today: fixed green (CCG List), fixed yellow (LighthouseFriends), continuous yellow (Lighthouse Directory). Focal height 8.1 m (CCG); 31 ft (9.4 m) above high water in 1903.

structures.type: square pyramidal wood tower with lantern and gallery, white with red trim and a red vertical stripe
structures.note: Height disputed: 9.1 m (30 ft) to the top of the lantern ventilator in 1904; 8 m (27 ft) in the Lighthouse Directory; 7.1 m structure height on the CCG List.

structures.name: Caraquet Range Rear (2)
structures.type: square cylindrical skeletal tower, white daymark with red vertical stripe
structures.note: Erected by the Canadian Coast Guard in 2000 (LighthouseFriends; Lighthouse Directory). CCG List: 226 degrees, 1091.4 m from the front light.

structures.name: Caraquet Range Rear (1), relocated
structures.type: square white wood tower with lantern and gallery
structures.note: The 1903 rear tower; inactive since 2000. Given to the Town of Bas-Caraquet and moved to a municipal park at the foot of Rue Lanteigne. Roofed patio added.

staffing.note: Keepers named to 1961 (LighthouseFriends). The date of automation is not in the sources read. The CCG List marks both range lights seasonal.

access.note: Front light at the end of a private lane off Route 145 in Bas-Caraquet. Grounds and tower closed.

visit.note: Front light viewable from Route 145 and the beach. Rear light: site and tower closed, easily seen from the road. Old 1903 rear tower in a municipal park: grounds open, tower closed.

events.note: Contract for the range towers given to J. R. Chiasson of Lower Caraquet, who could not do the work. John Kelly, Inspector of Lights, completed it.
Two wooden range towers erected at Lower Caraquet.
Put into operation 24 September 1903. Fixed white light, dioptric, seventh order, 31 ft (9.4 m) above high water.
Canadian Coast Guard erects an 11.3 m (37 ft) skeletal rear range tower.
Old 1903 rear tower given to the Town of Bas-Caraquet and moved to a municipal park. Inactive since 2000.

keepers.name: Theodore DeGrace
keepers.note: Front range light, 1925 to 1961 (LighthouseFriends only). The Marine reports in the corpus end in 1924, so this is not checked.

keepers.name: Patrice L. Legere
keepers.note: First keeper of the back range light (LighthouseFriends). Named against the Caraquet Back Range Light in the Department's list published 1906-07.

keepers.name: P.A. Lantaigne
keepers.note: Back range light, from 1913 to at least 1923 (LighthouseFriends). The 1915-16 keeper table has 'P. A. Lantaigne' with the date 27 March 1913; the station is not printed beside the name in the OCR. Also spelled Lanteigne or Lantaigne in other sources.

corrections.why: The current point is the 1903 rear tower, moved to a municipal park 1.3 km east (LighthouseFriends; Lighthouse Directory). The active 2000 rear range light is at 47 48 05.8 N, 064 51 06.0 W on the CCG List, 226 degrees and 1091.4 m from the front light.

corrections.proposed: 2000 rear range tower built and active; old 1903 rear tower relocated and inactive since 2000
corrections.why: Both 2000 events in the record belong to the two rear towers, not to the front range light, which the CCG List and the Lighthouse Directory show as active.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The record's 'inactive' reading is the Lighthouse Directory's entry for the old 1903 rear tower, inactive since 2000 and now a park feature. The front light is active on the CCG List and in the Lighthouse Directory's front entry.

notes_for_editor: Colour is unresolved. The CCG List gives F G (fixed green); LighthouseFriends says fixed yellow; the Lighthouse Directory says continuous yellow; Wikidata (in the record) gives F Y. The 1903 light was fixed white. Front tower height is also disputed: 9.1 m (30 ft) to the ventilator in the 1904 report, 8 m (27 ft) in the Lighthouse Directory, 7.1 m structure height on the CCG List, 8.0 m in the record. The 1903 focal height was 31 ft (9.4 m); the CCG gives 8.1 m now. Keeper names are from LighthouseFriends; the Marine keeper lists confirm Doucett (front, 1905 list) and Legere (back, 1906-07 list) by name on the same OCR line, but the 1915-16 table (J. O. Chaisson, 11 May 1912; P. A. Lantaigne, 27 March 1913) is OCR-split and its station column was not matched. Theodore DeGrace (1925 to 1961) is only in LighthouseFriends; the corpus ends in 1924. The Marine volume's corpus label is 1903 but its identifier is 1904 and it is cited as published 1904. Lantaigne is spelled three ways (LighthouseFriends P.A. Lantaigne; Marine G. Lantaigne; Lighthouse Directory Rue Lanteigne). The Pointe a Brideau range in Caraquet town (Lighthouse Directory: 1978, inactive since 2020) is a different range and is not this station. A Marine report line for 1909-10 reads 'Caraquet. The catoptric light has been replaced by a 360 degree 5th order French lens' with no qualifier; it is not clearly this range and is not used. No storm, wreck or rescue is tied to the range in the corpus or the sources read. Living people: DeGrace and Chaisson are named only as LighthouseFriends prints them, with no personal detail. Photos: none added; the record's Wikimedia photo licence is unknown.
